count_documents.description: Count matching documents and break the total down by month, agency, topic, document type or any other grouping, without fetching the documents themselves. This is how to answer 'which agencies published most about this?' or 'is this picking up?' in one step. Takes exactly the same filters as Search documents. No API key required.
count_documents.name: count_documents

parameters.description: What to group the counts by. Grouping by day over a long range returns a lot of rows, so pair it with a date range.
parameters.name: group_by

parameters.description: Optional. Words to look for in the full text of a document. Put a phrase in quotes to keep it together ("clean water"), and separate alternatives with a vertical bar to match any of them ("wildfire" | "prescribed burn"). Leave blank to match everything and rely on the filters below.
parameters.name: term

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents published by these agencies. The list comes from the Federal Register itself, so it is every agency that publishes: all 470-odd of them, departments and sub-agencies alike. Leave empty for every agency.
parameters.name: agencies

parameters.description: Optional. Only these kinds of document. A final rule is law; a proposed rule is what an agency intends to do and is usually open for comment; a notice is everything else an agency must announce; a presidential document is an executive order, proclamation or memorandum. Leave empty for all four.
parameters.name: document_types

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents published on or after this date. The Federal Register's online record starts in 1994. Set this and 'Published on or before' to the same day to read a single issue.
parameters.name: published_from

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents published on or before this date. Leave blank to run up to today.
parameters.name: published_to

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents indexed under these subject terms. These are the Code of Federal Regulations' own indexing terms, such as 'Air pollution control' or 'Motor vehicle safety', and are far more specific than the subject areas below. Leave empty for every topic.
parameters.name: topics

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents filed under these subject areas: the six broad headings FederalRegister.gov browses by. Use topics above for anything narrower. Leave empty for all six.
parameters.name: sections

parameters.description: Whether to narrow to the rules deemed significant under Executive Order 12866, which are the ones that went through White House review before being published. Both by default.
parameters.name: significance

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents that take effect on or after this date. A rule is usually published weeks before it takes effect, so this is the date to filter on when the question is 'what changes soon?' rather than 'what was announced?'.
parameters.name: effective_from

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents that take effect on or before this date.
parameters.name: effective_to

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents filed under this agency docket, which is how a single rulemaking is followed from proposal to final rule. Every document reports its own docket numbers.
parameters.name: docket_id

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents carrying this Regulation Identifier Number, which the government assigns to a rulemaking and keeps for its whole life. Every document reports its own.
parameters.name: regulation_id_number

parameters.description: Optional. Only documents that change this title of the Code of Federal Regulations, the permanent rulebook the Federal Register amends. Leave blank for every title.
parameters.name: cfr_title

description: The daily journal of the United States government. Every rule, proposed rule, notice and presidential document a federal agency publishes appears in the Federal Register, and all of it since 1994 is here: search it by agency, subject, docket, RIN, part of the Code of Federal Regulations, or distance from a place; read a whole day's issue the way it is printed; count what is being published and by whom; and watch the public inspection desk to see what is coming before it appears. Every document carries the agency's own summary, the day it takes effect and the day comments close, so a workflow can raise an alert on a deadline that matters. Free and open: no account or API key required.
